title: Gajendra Singh v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Krishna Murari, J.; Prashant Kumar, J.
disposition: Recovery certificate dated 29.02.2016 quashed; writ allowed.
headnote: A recovery certificate issued without a prior provisional assessment, contrary to the mandatory procedure in clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, cannot be sustained and is liable to be quashed.
facts: The petitioner challenged a recovery certificate dated 29 February 2016 issued by the electricity authorities. He alleged that recovery had been started without a provisional assessment and without notice giving him a chance to object. On 29 April 2016 the Court stayed coercive action and called for instructions. At the final hearing, counsel for the distribution licensee fairly stated on instructions that no provisional assessment had been made before the recovery certificate issued.

reusable_constructions.construction: Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is mandatory; a recovery certificate issued without a prior provisional assessment is unsustainable.

holding_units.holding: In the absence of a provisional assessment and of compliance with clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which is mandatory, a recovery certificate is not liable to be sustained and is quashed.
